title: Guided onboarding initiative (Hosted API): in-console checklist + first production launch path
creator: Nikhil Sharma
description:
Initiative owner: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API onboarding) + Marissa Cole (Console checklist & rollout)
Exec sponsor: Alex Martinez

Summary
We will build a guided onboarding experience and in-product “first production launch” checklist to reduce time-to-first-success (TTFS) and make the path to production reliable, measurable, and repeatable for developers integrating the Hosted API.

Phase 1 scope (self-serve Hosted API)
- Console checklist UI (feature-flagged) with step state + deep links to canonical docs.
- Validation where feasible (automatic completion signals):
  - API key created
  - prod-mode key created / labeled
  - first successful request
  - first streaming session
  - visited usage dashboard (and/or basic observability interaction)
- Checklist content: define “first production launch” minimum safeguards and recommended best practices.
- SDK + quickstart alignment across Python/TypeScript/Go so each checklist step has a canonical, copy-consistent code path.
- Onboarding telemetry: stable event schema + internal dashboards to measure completion funnel, drop-off, and correlation with retention/usage.
- Privacy/security review for telemetry (no customer prompt content, property allowlist, retention tagging, access controls).

Out of scope (Phase 1)
- Dedicated / Private deployment onboarding (follow-on initiative).
- Deep identity onboarding (SSO/SAML).
- Automated validation for every production-readiness item (we’ll validate a subset; the rest are educational + docs-driven).

Primary goals (what success looks like)
1) Faster activation:
   - Reduce median time from signup → first successful API response.
   - Reduce median time from signup → first “production launch” completion (as defined below).
2) Higher completion rates:
   - Increase checklist completion rate for new orgs exposed to the experience.
   - Reduce step drop-off at historically high-friction points (API keys, auth errors, 429 confusion, streaming stability).
3) Measurable, stable instrumentation:
   - Event schema v1 implemented end-to-end; dashboarding and alerting in place to detect telemetry regressions.

Target personas
- Self-serve engineers integrating an LLM into a product feature (often under time pressure, minimal ML infra support).
- Common patterns: copy/paste quickstart, then productionize with retries/timeouts, quotas, and monitoring.

Working definition: “First production launch” (Phase 1)
Production launch is defined as: a project has (a) a prod-mode API key, (b) at least one successful request from a non-local environment (or a flagged environment tag), and (c) minimum safeguards configured.

Minimum safeguards (required for checklist completion of the production section)
- Use prod-mode key (or explicitly labeled key) and store it outside source control.
- Configure timeouts + retries with backoff (SDK defaults where available).
- Understand quota/rate limit behavior and have basic 429 handling.
- Have minimal observability: ability to view usage/latency/errors in Console (and recommended request-id correlation).
- Rollback/fallback guidance acknowledged (educational step; not fully auto-validated in Phase 1).

Milestones & timeline (target)
Discovery (2–3 weeks)
- Funnel analysis + baseline metrics
- Support/CS ticket review (401, 429, streaming disconnects, CORS)
- Customer/prospect interviews (what “prod-ready” means, what steps should be validated)

Definition (2 weeks)
- PRD + UX spec finalized
- Checklist step list + copy locked for Beta
- Event schema v1 approved + privacy review started

Build (4–6 weeks)
- Console checklist UI + backend state model
- Validators for “first successful request” and “first streaming session”
- API key UX updates (prod vs test)
- Docs IA updates + deep links (version-stable URLs + UTM conventions)
- Quickstart/SDK snippet parity for Python/TS/Go
- Telemetry pipeline + dashboards + alerts

Beta (2–3 weeks)
- Feature-flagged rollout to subset of new signups + select existing accounts
- Weekly review of funnel + qualitative feedback
- Iterate on copy/ordering and fix instrumentation gaps

GA (1–2 weeks)
- Broader rollout
- Release notes + internal enablement (Support macros, CS guidance)
- Post-launch retro and follow-up backlog

Success metrics (v1)
Activation / speed
- TTFS: median and p75 time from signup → first successful API response (per project).
- TTFP: median and p75 time from signup → “first production launch” completion.

Funnel / completion
- Checklist view → step1 complete → first request → streaming step → prod key → production section complete.
- Step-level drop-off rate and time-between-steps.

Quality / reliability
- Reduction in top onboarding support contacts per 1k signups (401 wrong key env, 429 confusion, streaming disconnects).
- Telemetry health SLO: event delivery latency and missing-event rate (alerted).

Guardrails / privacy
- Zero collection of customer prompt content in onboarding telemetry.
- Property allowlist + redaction rules enforced at emit points.

Launch criteria (Beta → GA)
Product/UX
- Checklist renders for flagged cohort with accessible interaction patterns (keyboard navigation, screen reader labels, contrast).
- Step state is stable across sessions/devices (server-side persistence) with clear “last updated” indicators.
- Copy and deep links match docs canonical URLs; no broken links; back-navigation pattern validated.

Engineering / reliability
- Feature flag targeting supports: new orgs, allowlist, % rollout, admin override.
- Validators:
  - “First successful request” signal: accurate enough for onboarding purposes (documented lag/edge cases).
  - “First streaming session” signal: resilient to disconnect/retry edge cases; does not double-complete.
- E2E tests cover: flag on/off, state persistence, validator-driven completion, reset/admin override.

Telemetry & analytics
- Event schema v1 shipped with required properties and dedupe keys.
- Dashboards live (completion funnel + telemetry health) and used in weekly beta review.
- Alerts configured for missing events / pipeline delays / sharp drop-offs.

Security/Privacy
- Security + legal/privacy review signed off (retention tags, access controls, no prompt content).
- Documentation for what is collected and why, plus retention period documented.

Support readiness
- Support playbook updated with checklist references and troubleshooting links.
- At least 2 weeks of beta issues triaged with clear escalation path and owners.

Key risks / notes
- Validator lag: “first successful request” based on gateway logs/metrics may lag by minutes; UX must set expectations.
- Over-validating: avoid blocking users on hard-to-detect items (rollbacks, observability integrations). Prefer “recommended” steps.
- Deep links drift: docs URLs/versioning must be stable; require redirect ownership.
- Telemetry privacy: must keep schema minimal; avoid capturing any user text or customer identifiers beyond approved allowlist.

Artifacts
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/guided-onboarding-checklist-prd-2026-01.json
- UX spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-guided-onboarding-ux-spec-2026-01.json
- ADR (state + validation): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0137-onboarding-checklist-state-and-validation.json
- Event schema: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/onboarding-telemetry-event-schema-v1.json
- First production launch checklist (internal): sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/first-production-launch-checklist.json
- Docs IA update: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/onboarding-info-architecture-update-2026.json
- Rollout runbook: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/console-checklist-feature-flag-rollout.json

Open questions (to close before GA)
- Do we consider “production” to require a non-test key only, or also a non-local origin / environment tag?
- What is the minimum acceptable accuracy for the first-request validator (esp. multi-project orgs)?
- Which steps are required vs recommended in Console, and how do we represent that visually?
- Final UTM conventions and attribution model for doc deep links.
- Retention period for onboarding telemetry and who can access raw events vs aggregated dashboards.
